channel.title: Research \ Anthropic
channel.description: Unofficial RSS feed scraped from https://www.anthropic.com/research

item.title: Scenarios for our economic future
item.description: The Anthropic Economics Team models the effects of AI on the economy of 2030.

item.title: How Claude is uplifting biomolecular modeling
item.description: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

item.title: Illuminating the frontier
item.description: Today, the world can’t see what’s going on inside AI labs. Anthropic is proposing new metrics that would give the public visibility into frontier AI development.

item.title: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats
item.description: In early results from our new life sciences research lab, Claude agents found an enzyme system whose function is still unknown.

item.title: Project Swap: What happens when agents trade for us?
item.description: To see what works and what breaks when agents are sent into a market, we made a miniature market of Claudes.

item.title: Yes, Claude can do Nine Loops
item.description: Claude computes a nine-loop amplitude in N=4 super-Yang-Mills

item.title: What do you want from AI?
item.description: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

item.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
item.description: GLM-5.3 can autonomously build end-to-end cyber exploits, but unlike other frontier models, it was released without meaningful safeguards to limit misuse.

item.title: What work can robots do?
item.description: What work can robots do? Anthropic's robot exposure index finds robots can do 3/4 of US physical job tasks, but are cost-competitive for only 0.3%.

item.title: Claude-shaped science
item.description: Matthew Schwartz describes what happened when he stopped fighting Claude and allowed Claude to find “Claude-shaped” problems. This led him to build BootLoops, a toolkit for exact calculations in quantitative science, which he has been applying across scientific fields alongside experts.

item.title: The missing map of the sky
item.description: Claude Science helped produce the first complete map of the sky in UV light

item.title: Launching an opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software
item.description: We’re launching OSS Scanner, an opt-in vulnerability scanner for the open-source ecosystem informed by our experience using Claude to find vulnerabilities during Project Glasswing. Projects that join will receive thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost.

item.title: Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use
item.description: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

item.title: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
item.description: Small AI models may be only months away from being able to self-replicate across cheap IoT devices like Android TV boxes, with no datacenter needed.

item.title: Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks
item.description: Illicit distillation allows model developers to copy frontier AI capabilities without creating proportionally robust safeguards. Here, we describe how we’ve reduced the rate of distillation by more than 90%.

item.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
item.description: As our merges per day grew more than tenfold, source control became our biggest development bottleneck. Here, we share how we migrated to an in-house version control system in five months.

item.title: Working at the frontier shapes expectations for the future
item.description: We’re sharing two reports: the first covers how AI is changing employment inside Anthropic, and the second looks at the gap between how the public and Anthropic employees expect AI to affect work and the economy.

item.title: How employment is changing at Anthropic
item.description: How has AI restructured work and employment at Anthropic? As a company at the frontier of AI adoption, Anthropic could be a leading indicator of how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy.

item.title: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins
item.description: The decades-old mystery of the origins of one of the most popular cryptographic standards has been explained.

item.title: Designing more efficient quantum circuits with Claude
item.description: Working largely on its own, Claude designed quantum circuits that improve on the best published versions, in some cases by an order of magnitude or more.

item.title: The AI expectations gap
item.description: How will AI reshape the economy in the years ahead? What is the core source of disagreement about AI's future impact on the economy? This note presents new survey evidence on these questions.

item.title: How Claude designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins
item.description: We asked an internal research Claude model to design minibinders (small proteins that attach tightly to a target) against scorpion neurotoxins.

item.title: An alignment assessment of the UK AISI cybertesting incident
item.description: In a UK AISI evaluation, Mythos 5 took unsanctioned actions that impacted real people and organizations. In this post, we investigate these behaviors from Claude Mythos 5 further, to understand what they reveal about the model’s alignment.

item.title: How AI agents shape experts’ judgment calls
item.description: In a randomized trial, professional analysts working with an AI coding agent went with the option the agent was randomly assigned to favor 86% of the time. We look at what this means for human oversight of AI-assisted work.

item.title: Early progress on accelerating drug development with Claude
item.description: Over the past several months, we’ve partnered with six organizations to accelerate curing disease. We’ve also started drug discovery efforts of our own, including programs for rare childhood forms of muscular dystrophy. In this post, we provide an update on our progress.

item.title: Progress on provable inference for large language models
item.description: Sharing progress on a powerful type of cryptographic proof known as a zkSNARK, which is uniquely fit for provable inference.

item.title: Investigating vault particles with Claude
item.description: We’re sharing another finding from Anthropic’s biology research lab: the first 3D structure of a vault particle found in prokaryotic cells.

item.title: AI for scientific discovery: How researchers use Claude
item.description: We analyzed 207,000 research sessions to learn how Claude is used in science, why some tasks get more use than others, and how AI could speed up discovery.

item.title: The components of agent memory
item.description: For Claude to learn from experience, it has to decide what’s worth remembering before it knows what’s next. Here’s how “dreaming” helps it organize memory and correct mistakes.

item.title: Teaching AI to build scientific models
item.description: AI for Science grantees Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon, and Stefan Wahl on how AI is starting to change how scientific models are built and interpreted.

item.title: Testing Claude on real-world electronics design
item.description: We asked Claude to design three electronic devices: a speakerphone, a voice-assistant hub, and a handheld virtual pet. The prototypes worked without any fixes to their circuitry.
